Delta Leakage Sensitivity Index (Delta LSI)

Source: R/delta_lsi.R
delta_lsi.Rd

Compares a naive (potentially leaky) cross-validation pipeline against a guarded (leakage-protected) pipeline and quantifies leakage-induced performance inflation using the Leakage Sensitivity Index (LSI).

Usage

delta_lsi(
  fit_leaky,
  fit_guarded,
  metric = "auc",
  exchangeability = c("iid", "by_group", "within_batch", "blocked_time"),
  learner = NULL,
  higher_is_better = NULL,
  block_size = NULL,
  M_boot = 2000L,
  M_flip = 10000L,
  strict = FALSE,
  return_details = FALSE,
  seed = 42L,
  ...
)

Arguments

fit_leaky

A LeakFit object from the leaky (unprotected) evaluation pipeline.

fit_guarded

A LeakFit object from the guarded (leakage-protected) evaluation pipeline.

metric

Character. Performance metric to compare. Must appear in fit@metrics of both fits (e.g., "auc", "rmse").

exchangeability

Character. One of "iid" (default), "by_group", "within_batch", "blocked_time". Stored and reported; all settings use the same corrected t-test, because the correction already accounts for the dependence these settings used to address. For "by_group" / "within_batch" the number of group / batch levels is reported in info$n_groups_used / info$n_batches_used. Earlier versions ran sign-flip tests here that were anti-conservative with real model fits.

learner

Optional character. Learner name to select from multi-learner fits. If NULL, the first learner found in fit@metrics is used.

higher_is_better

Logical or NULL. Whether a higher value of metric indicates better performance. When NULL (default), auto-detected from the metric name: names containing "rmse", "mse", "mae", "mape", "mase", "log_loss", "brier", "error", "loss", "deviance" or "cost" are lower-is-better; names such as "auc", "accuracy", "f1", "kappa", "rsq" or "cindex" are higher-is-better; any other name warns and is treated as higher-is-better. Setting this correctly ensures that a positive delta_lsi always indicates leakage inflation (the naive pipeline is artificially more optimistic than the guarded one).

block_size

Ignored; retained for compatibility (a warning is issued when supplied).

M_boot

Ignored; retained for compatibility (no bootstrap is used).

M_flip

Ignored; retained for compatibility (no sign-flip test is used).

strict

Logical. If TRUE, error on insufficient R_eff instead of a warning.

return_details

Logical. If TRUE, include the per-repeat \(\Delta_r\) vector, the paired fold deltas and the original fit objects in the info slot.

seed

Ignored; retained for compatibility (the method is deterministic).

...

Unused. Reserved for deprecated aliases such as fit_naive.

Value

A LeakDeltaLSI object. Use summary() to print a formatted report. For programmatic access to inflation estimates, confidence intervals, p-values, tier labels, and the per-repeat fold-level deltas, use the S4 accessor methods registered for LeakDeltaLSI:

  • dlsi_metric(dlsi) – raw mean of per-repeat metric differences (the delta_metric slot).

  • dlsi_robust(dlsi) – Huber-robust point estimate (the delta_lsi slot).

  • dlsi_ci(dlsi, which = "robust" | "metric") – corrected-t 95% confidence interval for either the robust or the raw estimate.

  • dlsi_p_value(dlsi) – corrected repeated-CV t-test p-value.

  • dlsi_tier(dlsi) – inference-tier label ("A_full_inference", "B_signflip_ci", "C_signflip", or "D_insufficient").

  • dlsi_R_eff(dlsi) – effective number of independent units (folds per repeat).

  • dlsi_repeats(dlsi, which = "naive" | "guarded") – per-repeat metric data frame for the requested pipeline.

The full list of accessor methods for the class is available through methods(class = "LeakDeltaLSI").

Details

Method

For each fit, per-fold metric values are extracted from fit@metrics (or recomputed from fit@predictions if necessary). Fold test-set sizes are used as weights to aggregate fold metrics into per-repeat estimates \(\mu_r\). The repeat-level delta \(\Delta_r = s \cdot (\mu_r^{\text{naive}} - \mu_r^{\text{guarded}})\) captures leakage-induced performance inflation for each CV repeat, where \(s = +1\) for higher-is-better metrics (e.g., AUC) and \(s = -1\) for lower-is-better metrics (e.g., RMSE), so that \(\Delta_r > 0\) always indicates the naive pipeline is more optimistic than the guarded one.

The delta_lsi point estimate is the Huber M-estimator (k = 1.345) applied to \(\{\Delta_r\}\), which is robust to occasional outlier repeats. delta_metric is the arithmetic mean of \(\{\Delta_r\}\) for easy interpretation in the original metric's units.

Pairing requires that fit_leaky and fit_guarded share identical fold structures (same test-set membership per fold). When fold structures differ, a warning is issued and the fits are treated as unpaired. Folds whose metric is missing in either fit are dropped from both before pairing, so the paired delta always compares the same test sets.

Inference uses a corrected repeated cross-validation t-test on the paired fold deltas \(d_j\), with folds that re-use an identical test set (e.g. repeated leave-one-batch-out) averaged into one, so \(J\) counts distinct test sets. Repeated CV re-partitions the same data, so fold deltas are correlated through overlapping training sets and across repeats; treating them (or the repeats) as independent gives badly anti-conservative tests. The variance of the mean is corrected as \((1/J + n_{\text{test}}/n_{\text{train}})\, s_d^2\) (Nadeau & Bengio, 2003), and the t reference uses \(k - 1\) degrees of freedom, where \(k\) is the number of folds per repeat (calibrated degrees of freedom, Bouckaert, 2003): repeats sharpen the estimate but add no independent information. The test statistic is delta_metric / se; the 95% CIs for delta_metric and delta_lsi are the estimate \(\pm t_{0.975, k-1}\, se\). In simulations with real model fits under \(H_0\) (subject-grouped, batch-blocked and leave-one-study-out designs, 1-20 repeats) the type-I error stayed at or below the nominal 5%; with 3-fold designs (2 df) the test is conservative.

R_eff is the number of folds per repeat \(k\) (for study_loocv, the number of studies), the number of effectively independent units.

Inference tiers

Tier labels are kept from earlier versions for compatibility; every tier except D reports a p-value and both CIs.

"A_full_inference"

R_eff >= 20

"B_signflip_ci"

10 <= R_eff < 20

"C_signflip"

3 <= R_eff < 10

"D_insufficient"

R_eff < 3 or unpaired: point estimate only

inference_ok is TRUE whenever a finite p-value and CI were computed.

References

Nadeau, C. and Bengio, Y. (2003). Inference for the generalization error. Machine Learning, 52, 239-281.

Bouckaert, R. R. (2003). Choosing between two learning algorithms based on calibrated tests. Proceedings of ICML 2003, 51-58.
